rationale: After the Asian open the NQ book is thin and few people trade it, so a price that pokes through a level where stops are known to rest (the prior day's, the five-day, the swing or equal highs and lows, all taken together) and closes back inside has taken those stops with no real buyer or seller behind the move, and it drifts back; the main setting is how early in the evening the fade may start. Losing side: The traders whose resting stops sit behind the prior day, five-day and swing highs and lows, and the breakout buyers and sellers who chase a poke through them in the thinnest book of the day.
notes: liq: the highs and lows of the prior day, overnight, Asia, London, the evening before, the last 5 days and the last untraded swing (50 5-minute bars each side) and, on NQ, equal highs / lows are liquidity levels -> sweep = a bar trades beyond one and closes back inside: fade it; break = the first close beyond it: follow it; one signal per price per session
note: idea nq_asia_liq_sweep: the locked variants on the test days with worse fills (2 ticks + 250 ms), session eve
